out_of_scope_observations.observation: Pre-existing symlinks at cp-state paths are NOT scrubbed by Iter-2's ln -sf scanner (which only blocks subagent CREATION of new symlinks via Bash). spec-check.py uses path.read_text() / path.write_text() without O_NOFOLLOW or lstat-then-open(O_NOFOLLOW) — would silently follow a symlink introduced by a different vector (filesystem-layer manipulation, prior compromised state). This is residual risk OUT-OF-SCOPE for cycle 2 because (i) the cooperative-but-buggy threat model does not include adversarial symlink injection from non-Bash vectors, AND (ii) spec-check.py hardening would touch read_text/write_text call sites and is a separate defense-in-depth cycle. Recorded for future-cycle visibility per QA revision #6.

root_cause_analysis.symptom: 13 Bash-write forms (4 codex reproducer + 9 codex-this-cycle high-risk) directly write to cp-state-*.json files while pretool-cp-state-write-guard.py returns rc=0.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: The guard hook delegates Bash-target extraction to lib.bash_write_targets.extract_bash_write_paths, which returns raw post-operator path tokens (relative or absolute) without (a) post-cd cwd resolution and (b) cp/mv/install/rsync to-directory dest-basename synthesis. The structural cp-state matcher (cycle 1's _is_cp_state_components) then sees either a relative path with no spec-dir prefix or a destination directory with no cp-state basename — neither matches the structural shape parts[-3]=='specs' + basename cp-state-*.json. Additionally, several natural-shell write idioms (ln -sf, python -c open, dd of=, curl -o, wget -O, &>, git checkout --, touch) are not parsed by the shared extractor at all, so their target paths never reach the structural matcher.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — the gap predates cycle 1; it is a structural limitation of the regex-based extractor and is documented in cycle 1's qa-report-20260507-142952.json out-of-scope observations and in close-report-20260507-142952.md Round 1b' codex evidence
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The shared extractor was designed for a smaller threat model: catching write-redirects to known-bad path prefixes via tool-policy. Cycle 1 piggybacked the cp-state guard on the same extractor, inheriting the extractor's gaps. The path-component normalization fix in cycle 1 (L4 layer) does not help for paths that never reach the normalizer (L3 extraction layer fails first).
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Subagents (cooperative-but-buggy) may naturally produce any of these 13 forms when attempting to manipulate cp-state JSON. A guard that blocks 1/N attack surfaces leaves the remaining N-1 surfaces open — partially-effective security boundary equals no security boundary against a misbehaving subagent that stumbles into one of the open forms.
